prompt: What question does a regression test ask of a candidate release?

choices.text: Whether customers will like it
choices.why: That is production's question, after release.

choices.text: Whether its average beats the last release's
choices.why: An average can rise while a case breaks.

choices.text: How fast its model answers
choices.why: Time is reported, not the question.

choices.text: What it changed, case by case
choices.why: Right. Not whether it is good.

prompt: Why do the candidates in releases.json start in 2099?

choices.text: So they are priced at a future price
choices.why: The runs are priced at today's prices.

choices.text: So nothing in production picks them up
Because a release needs a date after the set's
So that regress.py sorts them last

prompt: Match each candidate to what it changes.
Comparing 2026.09.4 with 2026.10.1, how many cases broke?
Why was the floor release cheaper and faster?

choices.text: Its model was a smaller one
It cached the replies from the week before
It refused more questions
choices.why: Right. A refusal is short and calls no model: the savings were unanswered questions.

choices.text: The price of extract-1 fell on 1 October

prompt: What is the first rule of reading a regression report, from the release that shipped?

choices.text: Read cost and latency beside the broken cases
A faster release is a better release
choices.why: This one was faster because it answered less.

choices.text: Ignore the held-out split until the end
choices.why: True of tuning, not the rule this report teaches.

choices.text: Only a significant p-value counts
choices.why: Five broken cases at p = 0.0625 still block it.

prompt: In a paired comparison, which cases carry the information?

choices.why: They say nothing about the difference.

choices.text: The held-out ones

prompt: Five changed cases, all broken. What is the exact two-sided McNemar p-value?

choices.text: Because 0.0625 rounds down to 0.05
choices.why: It does not, and that is not the reason.

choices.text: Because McNemar is the wrong test here
choices.why: It is the right one for paired verdicts.

choices.text: Because the held-out split was not run
choices.why: It ran: two of the five are held out.

choices.text: Five customer questions broke
choices.why: Right. A broken case is a fact, not a statistic.
